title: Why Ice Cream Gives You Brain Freeze
sources: Serrador JM et al., "Cerebral blood flow during sphenopalatine ganglion stimulation (brain freeze)", FASEB Journal 26 (2012)
Mages S et al., "Experimental provocation of 'ice-cream headache' by ice cubes and ice water", Cephalalgia 37 (2017)
Harvard Health Publishing, "Brain freeze: what it is and how to stop it"

lines.text: If you eat ice cream too fast,
lines.caps: If you eat | ice cream | too fast,

lines.text: you might get a sudden, stabbing pain right behind your forehead.
lines.caps: you might get | a sudden, | stabbing pain | right behind | your forehead.

lines.text: It's called brain freeze, but your brain isn't actually freezing.
lines.caps: It's called | brain freeze, | but your brain | isn't actually | freezing.

lines.text: When something ice cold touches the roof of your mouth,
lines.caps: When something | ice cold | touches the roof | of your mouth,

lines.text: it chills the blood vessels running just above it.
lines.caps: it chills | the blood vessels | running just | above it.

lines.text: and the arteries feeding your brain suddenly widen,

lines.text: rushing in warm blood to protect it.
lines.caps: rushing in | warm blood | to protect it.

lines.text: But that sudden rush raises the pressure inside your head,

lines.text: and the nerves there read it as a stabbing headache.

lines.text: The good news is that it's harmless, and it fades within a minute or two.

lines.text: And to make it stop even faster,

lines.text: press your tongue against the roof of your mouth, and warm it back up.
